stemMd: In a laboratory in Turin, 300 g of water at 10 °C is poured into 200 g of water at 60 °C in a well-insulated container. Ignore any heat exchanged with the container and the surroundings. What is the final temperature of the mixture?
explanationMd:
With no heat lost, the heat given up by the hot water equals the heat taken in by the cold water. Both are water, so the specific heat $c$ cancels and the equation only needs masses and temperature changes.

$$300\,(T-10) = 200\,(60-T)$$

$$300T - 3000 = 12000 - 200T \;\Rightarrow\; 500T = 15000 \;\Rightarrow\; T = 30\ ^{\circ}\text{C}.$$

**Check.** The cold water warms by 20 °C, and 300 × 20 = 6000. The hot water cools by 30 °C, and 200 × 30 = 6000. The exchanges match. The result is also closer to 10 °C than to 60 °C, as it must be, because there is more cold water than hot water.

distractorRationale.c: Gives the temperature rise of the cold water (30 - 10 = 20 °C) rather than the final temperature. The question asks for the temperature the mixture reaches.
distractorRationale.b: Takes the plain average of 10 °C and 60 °C. That would be right only for equal masses; here the larger mass of cold water pulls the result below 35 °C.
distractorRationale.a: Swaps the masses, so that the 200 g is treated as the cold water. The final temperature lies nearer the temperature of the larger mass, which is the cold one.
distractorRationale.d: Gives the difference between the two starting temperatures (60 - 10 = 50 °C). That is a gap between temperatures, not the temperature the mixture settles at.

accessibilityText: A calorimetry question. 300 grams of water at 10 degrees Celsius are poured into 200 grams of water at 60 degrees Celsius in a well insulated container, with no heat exchanged with the surroundings. The final temperature is wanted. The choices are 20, 30, 35, 40 and 50 degrees Celsius.

provenance.notes: Original item. Answer 30 degrees Celsius; every wrong choice is a real slip (temperature rise, plain mean, swapped masses, temperature difference).

review.author: polito-til-i-wave6-physics-technical-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: T = (300*10 + 200*60)/500 = 15000/500 = 30 °C. 35 °C is the plain average of the two temperatures, and 40 °C weights the masses the wrong way round. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tili-phys-tech-run9) reached the same answer: Weighted mean: (300*10+200*60)/500 = 15000/500 = 30 C. 35 is the simple average; 40 swaps masses; 20 and 50 are other slips.]
